title: MoS 2 -CNT hybrid electrodes with enhanced ion transport and capacitive charge storage for lithium-ion batteries and supercapacitors
content: Developing multifunctional electrode materials with high-rate performance and long-term cycling durability is crucial for advanced lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and supercapacitors (SCs). Herein, a MoS2-carbon nanotube (CNT) composite was synthesized via a hydrothermal method, forming conformally wrapped MoS2 nanosheets on conductive CNT networks with strong interfacial coupling. This well-integrated architecture enhances electron transport, accommodates volume variations, and promotes a dominant capacitive charge-storage contribution. When evaluated as a LIB anode, the composite achieved a reversible capacity of 1726 mAh g−1 over 100 cycles at 100 mAg−1, accompanied by a coulombic efficiency of nearly 100%. Structural analyses using XRD and HRSEM confirmed intimate MoS2-CNT interfaces and excellent mechanical integrity. As a supercapacitor electrode, the MoS2-CNT composite attained a specific capacitance of 806.8 F g−1 at 2.4 A g−1. After 8600 charge–discharge cycles, the electrode retained 74.1% of its initial capacitance while maintaining a coulombic efficiency of 97.7%. The fabricated all-solid-state symmetric supercapacitor (ASSC) delivered a specific capacitance of 167.5 F g−1 at 1.52 A g−1, together with a maximum energy density of 23.3 Wh kg−1 and a peak power density of 1920 W kg−1. The device maintained 89.1% of its initial capacitance after 5000 cycles. Overall, the MoS2-CNT composite emerges as a structurally robust and electrochemically versatile electrode material bridging LIB and SC performance requirements.
